items.quote: Reports must be submitted to the Investigations Office, where they will be addressed in accordance with the Procedures to this Policy, which include an initial review as set out under section 4 of the Procedures to determine whether the allegations contained in the Report fall within UBC’s Jurisdiction to Investigate.
items.reason: The policy has its own dedicated reporting and investigation process managed by the Investigations Office.
The policy does not mention a commitment to make the policy text itself publicly available.

items.quote: Reports must be submitted in writing, and should set out the relevant details with regards to the alleged Sexual Misconduct.
items.reason: The policy mentions submitting reports to the Investigations Office but does not provide clear, concrete contact details or steps.

items.quote: An individual’s sexual reputation or history of sexual activity cannot be submitted as evidence to prove that it was likely that the individual provided Consent.
items.reason: The policy explicitly prohibits the submission of a complainant's sexual history as evidence.

items.quote: They are not adversarial processes and hearings will not be held as part of the investigatory process.
items.reason: The policy guarantees that hearings will not be held, protecting the complainant from direct face-to-face contact or cross-examination.

items.quote: However, this section does not prevent: 8.2.1 any participants in the Investigation from disclosing information about themselves, or information that they have obtained outside the Investigation;
items.reason: The policy explicitly states that participants are not prevented from disclosing information about themselves or their own experiences.

items.quote: UBC is committed to respecting the rights of those who Disclose to make their own decisions about accessing support services and assistance, making a Report, or pursuing external processes such as criminal or civil actions (whether instead of or in addition to pursuing UBC’s processes).
items.reason: The policy explicitly guarantees the survivor's right to choose between institutional and external processes.

items.quote: An individual who makes a Disclosure or Report will not be subject to actions for violating any applicable UBC policy, rules, or regulations related to alcohol or drug use at the time the alleged Sexual Misconduct occurred.
items.reason: The policy guarantees amnesty from disciplinary action for drug or alcohol use at the time of the incident.

items.quote: The Director of Investigations will set the timelines for each Investigation and may adjust the timelines in an Investigation at any time.
items.reason: Timelines are provided but are explicitly optional and adjustable at the discretion of the Director of Investigations.

items.quote: Assistance will be available to Members of the UBC Community who have Disclosed or Reported and may include: student residence re-location or short-term emergency student housing; class schedule changes; provision of academic concessions; emergency funding for students; safety planning; temporary work reassignment, location reassignment, or scheduling changes;
items.reason: Interim measures are available but their specific implementation is discretionary.

items.quote: student, defined as any person, including co-op and exchange students, registered or enrolled in any component of a for-credit academic or training program or course at UBC, or any class of learners designated by resolution of the Senate as students;
items.reason: The scope of the policy explicitly includes co-op students.

items.quote: The Director of Investigations will inform the Complainant of any disciplinary outcomes that the University Counsel has authorized the Director to disclose in accordance with section 7.5 of these Procedures.
items.reason: Informing the complainant of disciplinary outcomes is limited and requires authorization from University Counsel.

items.quote: Annually, UBC will publicly report, in the aggregate and without identifying personal information, the number of: requests for services received by the Sexual Violence Prevention and Response Offices; and Reports received by the Investigations Office;
items.reason: The policy commits to publishing annual aggregate reports of numbers.

items.quote: UBC is committed to reviewing this Policy at least once every three years, in consultation with students and such other Members of the UBC Community as UBC deems appropriate in accordance with the Regulatory Framework Policy (GA2).
items.reason: The policy requires review at least once every three years, which is longer than the two-year benchmark.

items.quote: UBC is committed to reviewing this Policy at least once every three years, in consultation with students and such other Members of the UBC Community as UBC deems appropriate in accordance with the Regulatory Framework Policy (GA2).
items.reason: Student consultation is required, but there is no requirement for at least 30% student representation on the review committee.

items.quote: UBC will offer training on a Trauma-informed Approach to persons, including administrative and academic decision makers, responsible for addressing Sexual Misconduct.
items.reason: The policy commits to offering trauma-informed training, but does not explicitly make it mandatory.

items.quote: UBC is committed to providing comprehensive and inclusive education, prevention, and response initiatives to address Sexual Misconduct.
items.reason: The policy commits to providing comprehensive education and prevention initiatives.
